name: The graded devotional practices of BhG 12.8–12

stages.name: karmaphala-tyāga
stages.gloss: relinquishing the fruit of all actions
stages.description: If unable even to do the Lord's work: resorting to his yoga, self-restrained, relinquish the fruit of all actions (12.11).

stages.name: matkarma-parama
stages.gloss: intent on work for the Lord
stages.description: If unable even in practice: be intent on work for the Lord; doing actions for his sake one attains perfection (12.10).

stages.name: abhyāsa-yoga
stages.description: If unable to fix citta steadily on him: seek to reach him by the yoga of practice (12.9).

stages.name: manas and buddhi in the Lord
stages.gloss: placing manas and buddhi in him
stages.description: Place manas in him alone; let buddhi enter him (12.8).

stages.name: dwelling in the Lord
stages.description: 'You will dwell in me alone thereafter' (12.8).

notes: The text states the four instructions from the highest downward (12.8, then 'if you cannot …' 12.9, 12.10, 12.11), each for one unable to do the previous; they are listed here upward from the most accessible, as the conditional sequence implies. 12.12 then ranks knowledge above practice, meditation above knowledge and relinquishing the fruit of actions above meditation, with peace following immediately on relinquishment — an order that does not coincide with 12.8–11, where relinquishment is the step for one unable to do the others; Śaṅkara reads 12.12 as praise (stuti) of relinquishment (recalled; see the notes of teaching 12.12), and the commentators take the ranking variously. Bands are interpretive and left to the interpretation layer.
